title: A letter to the team lead about the starter
thesis: The slow invisible part of the work decides the result, long before anyone sees it.

nodes.text: To the team lead who rewards visible output: here is something I learned from bread.

evidence.filled_by: brief audience: team leads who reward visible output over slow groundwork

nodes.text: What prompts the letter now, and who is the writer to this reader? A letter needs that relationship, and the brief doesn't give it.
The starter decides the loaf: weak starter, flat sour bread, and nothing at the oven fixes it. That's why the month of feeding it matters.

evidence.filled_by: transcript line 5: "If the starter is weak, the loaves come out flat and sour and nobody can fix that at the oven."
brief must_include.0: the month of feeding the starter

nodes.text: The eleven years of notebooks are the same patience at a longer scale.

evidence.filled_by: brief must_include.1: the eleven years of notebooks

nodes.text: Whose notebooks are they, and what do they record? The brief doesn't say.
Good judges see quality in the slow part: she knew he would be good before any result showed it.

evidence.filled_by: transcript line 9: "That was the moment she knew he would be good."

nodes.text: My ask: protect the unglamorous early work on your team, before it has anything to show.

evidence.filled_by: brief purpose: make readers protect the unglamorous early work on their teams
